title: ABS vs PVC: Drainage Material Basics
description: Selecting between ABS and PVC for DWV (Drain, Waste, and Vent) systems requires understanding their distinct physical properties and installation requirements. ABS is a black, rigid plastic pipe with high impact strength, installed using a single-step solvent cement process. PVC is a white, chemically resistant pipe requiring a two-step process using primer and solvent cement to dissolve and weld the joint faces together. Because these materials expand and contract at different rates and react differently to chemicals, they should never be intermixed or joined using standard solvent cement without approved transitioning techniques or adapters according to local plumbing code.

ABS vs PVC: Drainage Material Basics

Selecting between ABS and PVC for DWV (Drain, Waste, and Vent) systems requires understanding their distinct physical properties and installation requirements. ABS is a black, rigid plastic pipe with high impact strength, installed using a single-step solvent cement process. PVC is a white, chemically resistant pipe requiring a two-step process using primer and solvent cement to dissolve and weld the joint faces together. Because these materials expand and contract at different rates and react differently to chemicals, they should never be intermixed or joined using standard solvent cement without approved transitioning techniques or adapters according to local plumbing code.
